title: 384. Geometry, Spatial Thinking & Measurement: Reflection of Coordinate Figures
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Change the vertical coordinate sign under horizontal-axis reflection.
questions.question: Reflect \((3,4)\) in the horizontal axis. What is its image?
questions.explanation: Horizontal-axis reflection keeps the horizontal coordinate and negates the vertical one, giving \((3,-4)\).
questions.hint: Identify which coordinate measures distance from the reflecting axis.

questions.learningObjective: Change the horizontal coordinate sign under vertical-axis reflection.
questions.question: Reflect \((-2,5)\) in the vertical axis. What is its image?
questions.explanation: Vertical-axis reflection negates the horizontal coordinate and preserves the vertical one, giving \((2,5)\).
questions.hint: Keep the coordinate parallel to the axis unchanged.

questions.learningObjective: Interchange coordinates when reflecting in the diagonal.
questions.question: Reflect \((-3,7)\) in \(y=x\). What is its image?
questions.explanation: Reflection in \(y=x\) interchanges the coordinates, so \((-3,7)\) becomes \((7,-3)\).
questions.hint: Consider the coordinate rule for reflection in the main diagonal.

questions.learningObjective: Interchange and negate coordinates for negative-diagonal reflection.
questions.question: Reflect \((4,-1)\) in \(y=-x\). What is its image?
questions.hint: Reflection in this diagonal involves both interchange and sign changes.

questions.concept: Reflection in a shifted vertical line
questions.learningObjective: Use equal distances on opposite sides of a vertical mirror line.
questions.question: Reflect \((5,3)\) in \(x=2\). What is its image?
questions.explanation: The original horizontal coordinate is \(3\) units to the right of the mirror. The image is \(3\) units left, at \(x=-1\), with vertical coordinate \(3\).
questions.hint: Place the image equally far on the opposite side of the mirror line.

questions.concept: Reflection in a shifted horizontal line
questions.learningObjective: Reflect a point across a nonzero horizontal line.
questions.question: Reflect \((-4,2)\) in \(y=-1\). What is its image?
questions.explanation: The original point is \(3\) units above the mirror. Its image is \(3\) units below, at \(y=-4\), and keeps \(x=-4\).
questions.hint: Measure the vertical gap to the mirror before reversing it.

questions.learningObjective: Identify a point that lies on a specified reflecting line.
questions.question: Which point is unchanged by reflection in \(x=3\)?
questions.explanation: Points on the mirror line remain fixed. The point \((3,-5)\) has horizontal coordinate \(3\); the other point does not.
questions.hint: A fixed point must have zero perpendicular distance to the mirror line.

questions.learningObjective: Find a mirror line as the perpendicular bisector of corresponding points.
questions.question: Reflection maps \((1,2)\) to \((7,2)\). Which line is the mirror line?
questions.explanation: The mirror is the perpendicular bisector of the joining segment. Its midpoint is \((4,2)\), and the segment is horizontal, so the mirror is \(x=4\).
questions.hint: Find the midpoint and perpendicular direction of the joining segment.

questions.learningObjective: Translate a reflected segment into coordinate constraints.
questions.question: The segment from \((1,3)\) to \((4,3)\) is reflected in \(y=x\). Which description gives its image?
questions.explanation: Interchanging coordinates maps the endpoints to \((3,1)\) and \((3,4)\). The image is the stated vertical segment.
questions.hint: Reflect both endpoints before describing the entire segment.

questions.learningObjective: Substitute reflected coordinates into a line equation.
questions.question: The line \(y=2x+1\) is reflected in the horizontal axis. Which equation describes its image?
questions.explanation: An image point \((x,y)\) comes from \((x,-y)\). Thus \(-y=2x+1\), giving \(y=-2x-1\). Both slope and intercept change sign.
questions.hint: Apply the reflection to the whole equation, including its constant.
